# Drone Mapping Innovations in Construction

Bram Fennton: Welcome back to The Xanaly Sessions. Today, we’re diving into drone mapping innovations in construction sites, specifically how aerial surveying is transforming job site analytics. I’m thrilled to have Odalys Wenkcroft with us. She’s the lead engineer on the SkyGrid project, which has been pushing the envelope in autonomous drone surveys for rebar tying and safety monitoring. Odalys, thanks for joining.

Odalys Wenkcroft: Thanks, Bram. Happy to be here.

Bram Fennton: So, Odalys, can you give us a snapshot of how drone mapping has changed over the last couple of years?

Odalys Wenkcroft: Absolutely. Up until about 2021, most drone surveys were manual or semi-automated, relying heavily on human pilots and post-flight data stitching. SkyGrid introduced real-time 3D mapping algorithms that stitch data as drones fly, cutting survey time by 40%. For example, on a recent high-rise job in Vellum City, we completed full rebar layout scans in under 30 minutes—previously that took over two hours with ground crews.

Bram Fennton: That’s impressive. Any unexpected challenges?

Odalys Wenkcroft: Definitely. Early on, we grappled with varying light conditions. Shadows from nearby cranes distorted the 3D reconstructions. We developed adaptive exposure controls that adjust in milliseconds. It’s a small tweak but made a huge difference in data clarity.

Audience Member (from the back): How does the system handle safety monitoring?

Odalys Wenkcroft: Great question. We’ve integrated thermal imaging and AI to detect unsafe worker postures or unauthorized zone entries. In one case, the drone flagged a worker near an unstable scaffold, prompting a site manager alert that prevented a potential accident.

Bram Fennton: Fascinating stuff. Thanks for sharing these real-world insights, Odalys.
